archetypes.name: fixture-enumeration
archetypes.rationale: The plan scopes the fixture-update sweep as 'count ≈ 50 anchor lines per grep' without listing which assert_case_clean blocks need updating, leaving a concrete gap that could break CI if any fixture is missed.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan instructs updating every assert_case_clean fixture in scripts/test-lint-foreground-markers.sh that anchors on a top-level Family B writer, but provides only an approximate grep command rather than an enumerated list. Read the actual test file and identify every assert_case_clean block whose fence anchors on ship-pr.sh, run-step5-review.sh, run-step2-dispatch.sh, collect-agent-results.sh, or dispatch-plan-voters.sh, and verify the plan's update instructions cover all of them. Separately, check whether any existing assert_case (exit-1) fixture that already contains a wait line on one of those writers will gain new unexpected error lines from the three new checks, which could invalidate its pinned needle assertions even though the plan claims extra stderr lines are safe. The plan's 'verify per fixture before editing' instruction is the only guard here — assess whether it is specific enough to prevent a missed fixture from silently breaking CI. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: regex-vs-evidence
archetypes.rationale: Three ERE patterns drive the new lint checks; if any pattern fails to match the canonical shapes already present in the repo, the lint will produce false positives or false negatives on the nine existing fences the plan claims will still pass.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan proposes three specific ERE patterns: a backward-init check for monitor_rc= integer initialization, a logical-end-line check for || monitor_rc=$?, and a keyword-plus-bareword check for conditional branching on monitor_rc. Read the canonical fence blocks in skills/implement/SKILL.md, skills/research/SKILL.md, skills/design/SKILL.md, and any skills/shared/ references that embed top-level Family B writer invocations, and manually apply each proposed ERE to the actual text to confirm all nine claimed canonical fences would pass. Pay particular attention to whether the init-check ERE's strict integer-literal constraint (rejecting monitor_rc=$something) is too narrow or too broad relative to what the live fences actually contain, and whether the logical-end-line ERE correctly handles multi-line monitor invocations assembled via backslash continuation as they appear in the repo today. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
